questions.question: Name the only Female Muslim ruler of India.
questions.solution:
• Only Female Muslim Ruler: Razia Sultana
  • Fact: She was the daughter of Iltutmish and ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1236 to 1240.

questions.question: At the age of ______, Mahavira left home and went to live in a forest.
questions.solution:
• Mahavira's Renunciation: 30
  • Detail: At age 30, Vardhamana Mahavira left his royal life to seek enlightenment; he attained Kaivalya 12 years later.

questions.question: ho defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the second battle of Tarain in 1192 AD?
questions.solution:
• Second Battle of Tarain (1192): Muhammad Ghori
  • Outcome: Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan, marking the beginning of Turkish rule in North India.

questions.question: Who was the accused in the murder of Saunders in 1928?
questions.solution:
• Saunders Murder (1928): Bhagat Singh
  • Context: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev killed John Saunders to avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai.

questions.question: Who was the ruler of Mysore in 1761?
questions.solution:
• Mysore Ruler 1761: Hyder Ali
  • History: Hyder Ali overthrew the Wodeyar dynasty's authority to become the de facto ruler of Mysore.

questions.question: The practice of erecting megaliths began about ______ years ago.
questions.solution:
• Megaliths Timeline: 3000 years ago
  • Note: The practice of marking burial sites with large stones was prevalent in South India, the Deccan, and the North-east.

questions.question: The first railway line was from _______ to ________ in India in 1853.
questions.solution:
• First Railway Line (1853): Mumbai to Thane
  • Detail: The 34-km long line was inaugurated during the tenure of Lord Dalhousie.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct about Nagara or North Indian Temple Style Architecture?
questions.option_2: The garbhagriha is always located directly under the tallest tower.
questions.option_3: There was no Kalasha, the topmost part of the temple.
questions.option_4: There were no tower or shikhara.
questions.solution:
• Nagara Architecture: Garbhagriha under the tallest tower
  • Fact: In North Indian style, the 'Shikhara' is always positioned directly above the sanctum sanctorum (Garbhagriha).

questions.question: Kanishka was a ruler of ______ dynasty.
questions.solution:
• Kanishka's Dynasty: Kushana
  • Achievement: He is famous for convening the Fourth Buddhist Council and starting the Shaka Era (78 AD).

questions.question: Most Harappan seals made of _____.
questions.solution:
• Harappan Seals: Steatite
  • Material: Most seals were square or rectangular and made of soft river stone called steatite.

questions.question: In which year did the Bhopal Gas Tragedy take place?
questions.solution:
• Bhopal Gas Tragedy: 1984
  • Event: A lethal gas (Methyl Isocyanite) leak occurred at the Union Carbide plant on the night of Dec 2-3.

questions.question: In which year through the Indian Official Secrets Act was freedom of press curbed?
questions.solution:
• Official Secrets Act (1904): 1904
  • Context: Introduced by Lord Curzon to restrict the freedom of the press and increase government secrecy.

questions.question: What was the capital of the Satavahana Dynasty (60 BC - 225 AD)?
questions.solution:
• Satavahana Capital: Pratishthana
  • Note: Also known as Paithan (Maharashtra), it was the main center of power for the 'Lords of the Dakshinapatha'.

questions.question: Which of the following persons was a slave-generals of Alauddin Khalji (1296-1316 AD)?
questions.solution:
• Alauddin Khalji's General: Malik Kafur
  • History: Known as 'Hazar Dinari', he led the Sultanate's successful military campaigns into South India.

questions.question: In which state of India are Buddhist cave temples, Barabar Caves, located?
questions.solution:
• Barabar Caves: Bihar
  • Detail: These are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, dating back to the Mauryan Empire (Ashoka).

questions.question: Which Indian movement was started to look into the problems of indigo planters in the year 1917?
questions.solution:
• Champaran Satyagraha (1917): Champaran Satyagraha
  • Impact: Gandhi's first major movement in India, targeting the exploitative indigo plantation system.

questions.question: Who used the ancient texts to suggest that widows could remarry?
questions.solution:
• Widow Remarriage Advocate: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
  • Success: His efforts led to the passing of the Hindu Widow Remarriage Act in 1856.

questions.question: hich freedom fighter of India composed the song, ‘Saare Jahan Se Achha’?
questions.solution:
• Saare Jahan Se Achha: Muhammad Iqbal
  • Note: Originally published in 1904, it remains one of the most enduring patriotic songs of India.

questions.question:
hich of the following statements is correct?
I. Tipu Sultan is also known as the Tiger of Mysore.
II. Tipu Sultan ruled over Mysore from 1782 to 1799.
questions.solution:
• Tiger of Mysore: Both I and II
  • Tipu Sultan: He ruled from 1782–1799 and died defending his capital, Seringapatam.

questions.question: Pulakeshin II was a ruler of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Pulakeshin II: Chalukya
  • Fact: The most famous ruler of the Vatapi Chalukyas; he famously stopped Harshavardhana's southern expansion.

questions.question: Which of the following architectural styles had an entrance gateway called ‘gopuram’?
questions.solution:
• Gopuram Entrance: Dravidian architecture
  • Detail: Massive, ornate entrance towers (Gopurams) are a signature feature of South Indian temples.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers of Mewar was defeated by Babur in the Battle of Khanwa (1527 AD)?
questions.solution:
• Battle of Khanwa (1527): Rana Sanga
  • Mughal Era: Babur used the 'Tulughma' tactic to defeat the powerful Rajput confederacy.

questions.question: ijayalaya belonged to which dynasty of India?
questions.solution:
• Chola Founder: Vijayalaya
  • Note: He captured Thanjavur in the mid-9th century, laying the foundation for the Imperial Cholas.

questions.question: hich of the following statements about Paramhansa Mandalis is INCORRECT?
questions.option_1: It was founded in 1849 in Maharashtra.
questions.option_2: Its founders did not believe in God.
questions.option_3: They were primarily interested in breaking caste rules.
questions.option_4: They also advocated for widow remarriage and women's education.
questions.solution:
• Paramhansa Mandali Fact: Founders did not believe in God (Incorrect)
  • Correction: They were monotheistic (believed in one God) and focused on social reforms like breaking caste taboos.

questions.question: n 1929, Indian National Congress demanded complete independence under the presidentship of ______.
questions.solution:
• Purna Swaraj (1929): Jawaharlal Nehru
  • Session: At the Lahore Session, the INC declared 'Complete Independence' as its ultimate goal.
